blocks.heading: Barriers to international trade
blocks.text: Trade barriers can include tariffs, quotas, embargoes, administrative obstacles and incompatible requirements, while transport, language and payment difficulties can also impede trade. A tariff is a tax on imports; a quota limits quantity; an embargo prohibits specified trade. A tariff can protect a local producer by raising an imported rival’s price, but can also raise input or consumer costs. A quota is not another percentage tax. Describe a barrier’s mechanism and affected parties rather than assume protection benefits everyone.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A country taxes an imported product while a separate measure caps how many units may enter. The tax is a tariff and the quantity cap a quota. A local input user may face higher costs from protection that helps a competing producer.
